scoreRule: 1 point per automatically scored item or sequence position, and 1 point per teacher-reviewed written response; unverified local proposal
description: Original shorter EN/B2 independent Listening assessment draft. Teacher review is required before any use.

variant.goal: Understand how a public acceptance speech develops personal gratitude, family influences and ideas about continuing growth.

gist.title: Which broader idea links the speaker's award to his personal reflections?
options: Success is mainly a result of competition.
Public awards should replace personal goals.
Recognition becomes an occasion to reflect on gratitude and growth.
The audience should judge a career by its most famous role.
gist.why: He uses the award as a starting point for broader thanks and self-reflection.

gist.title: What effect does the speaker's movement between humour and seriousness have?
options: It makes personal beliefs approachable while retaining their emotional weight.
It removes the need to discuss any difficult experiences.
It suggests that the speaker cannot decide whom to thank.
It turns the speech into a criticism of the other nominees.
gist.why: His family anecdotes and thoughtful reflections work together rather than cancelling each other.

detail.title: Why does the speaker mention respected fellow nominees?
options: To explain how the voting system works.
To contrast his own achievement with younger actors.
To ask the audience to award them prizes later.
To acknowledge that the occasion celebrates work beyond his own.
detail.why: He directs attention to others instead of treating recognition as only personal.

detail.title: How is gratitude presented as more than a formal expression?
options: As something that becomes unnecessary after success.
As a way of recognising what one receives and influencing how one acts.
As proof that individual effort does not matter.
As a requirement to praise every person equally.
detail.why: His language about being thankful connects appreciation with a continuing response.

detail.title: Why is the story about a future version of himself significant?
options: It gives the audience an exact plan for the next ten years.
It suggests that goals should remain the same throughout life.
It presents self-development as an ongoing process rather than a finished state.
It demonstrates that his childhood ambitions have all been forgotten.
detail.why: He keeps the person he wishes to become ahead of his present self.

sequence: He begins by recognising other people on the night.
He connects his personal values to family memories.
He finishes by returning to a personal message about his direction in life.

facts.title: Name one family member whose influence the speaker discusses.
facts.criteria: Accept father or mother; assess meaning, not exact wording.

open.title: Explain how an example from the speech makes gratitude more personal than a simple list of names.
open.answer: His memories of family or specific colleagues connect gratitude with lived experiences rather than formal acknowledgements.
open.criteria: Give one identifiable personal anecdote plus a clear explanation of its emotional or rhetorical effect.
